text:
maria: heads-up — ran a long-running repro that shows INT8 KV pages slowly creeping memory on longctx workloads, plus a small eval hit (~1.7% rouge) after page-evict reuse kicks in :frowning:
alex: can you paste the short profiler dump?
jamie: if it's page reuse that's suspect, maybe our LRU bucket size for quantized pages is too small under longctx sampling.
maria: profiler snippet below (first 20 lines of hotpath):
```
[1704123456] kernel_select: matmul_int8_fast chosen for seq<=512
[1704123456] kv_cache: page_alloc count=2413 free=12 frag_ratio=0.37
[1704123456] kv_cache: int8_page_hits=8840 misses=2200 evictions=121
[1704123460] batching: avg_batch=2.1 target=3.0
[1704123464] mem: reserved=7.9G resident=8.1G working_set_grow=+140M
```
maria: note the working_set_grow line — it keeps increasing over long sessions.
sara: did you repro on BF16/FP16 for comparison?
maria: BF16 steady, FP16 slightly higher mem but no creeping. repro only triggers when int8 + longctx + our aggressive reuse policy are combined.
tim: maybe stale pointers during compaction of quantized slots. we changed compact path in last runtime change.
alex: which commit did you test?
maria: tested on commit `d2f8a3c` (kernel selector + reuse heuristic tweak) and also on `main` after merge. both reproduce.
jamie: can you share the test harness? short is fine.
maria: harness: longctx-sim with 40% prefix reuse, random token growth to 30k, mix of streaming/complete. config snippet: 
```
kv.paging.enabled=true
kv.reuse.policy=sampled_lru
kv.reuse.sample_rate=0.6
runtime.quant=int8
kernel.auto_select=true
```

sara: interesting that sampled_lru.sample_rate affects it. maybe we allow stale pages back into active set too eagerly.
tim: I can run ASAN-like checks for pointer reuse during compaction, but that'll only catch use-after-free, not fragmentation semantics.
alex: let's also capture a full vmmap and page table diff between start and +1h. add `/proc/<pid>/smaps` dumps every 5m.
maria: done — I've attached smaps snapshot references in our ticket. quick diff shows repeated allocation pattern in slabmap buckets used by int8 pages.
jamie: can we temporarily flip sample_rate to 0.2 on canary and run the same load to see if growth stops?
sara: also try `kv.reuse.policy=evict_if_reuse_lt=0.5` (threshold policy) — that will bias evictions for low-hit pages.
maria: I'll run two canaries: one with sample_rate=0.2, one with threshold-policy. starting now.
deploy-bot: canary deploy request queued for group: runtime-int8-canary, env: staging.
alex: while that's running, let's run the accuracy eval suite on a stored prompt set to measure the ~1.7% rouge drop correlation. include deterministic seeds.
maria: canary1 (sample_rate=0.2) memory growth flat after 45m :thumbsup: accuracy still shows 1.6% drop.
maria: canary2 (threshold-policy) memory growth flat and accuracy drop reduced to 0.3%.
jamie: that suggests our reuse policy is reintroducing quantized pages that were slightly degraded and cause generation drift. threshold policy avoids bringing them back.
sara: do we have a cheap metric for page-quality (e.g., average activation norm diff when rehydrated)? if so we could make reuse policy quality-aware.
tim: we can compute a tiny digest on eviction: store a 64-bit sketch of recent activations and compare on reuse. cheap and maybe effective.
alex: good idea. start with L1 norm delta sketch; tune threshold.
maria: summary: root cause = sampled_lru + aggressive sampling allowed low-quality int8 pages to reenter hot set -> accuracy drift; compaction bug may worsen mem bloat but canary suggests policy change stops growth. next steps: 1) add page-quality digest for reuse decisions (P1), 2) tighten sampled_lru defaults (P0), 3) add smaps-based memwatch to staging (P0).
sara: agreed. please open a formal PR with the config defaults and the canary logs.
maria: created ticket INF-1289 with logs + smaps + eval diffs. tagging @alex @jamie @tim.
alex: can we also add a micro-benchmark to CI that runs 1h longctx-int8 pass to catch regressions? maybe on nightly.
jamie: yes - add to perf-nightly only.
maria: cool. thanks all. I'll start a small prototype for the digest.
tim: ping me when prototype ready, I'll run compaction stress tests.
maria: will do. :rocket:
